title: Solar Radiation Eye Protection Simulator
description: A sunlight exposure simulation where the user positions protective sunglasses between a radiant godrays light source and a virtual sensor. The user adjusts lens tint darkness, UV filter strength, polarization angle, and distance from the light source, then runs a radiation analysis to evaluate eye safety ratings under varying solar intensities.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a solar radiation eye protection simulator. Load 'shared_assets/godrays_demo.glb' as the central radiant light source placed at world origin, and 'shared_assets/SunglassesKhronos.glb' positioned 3 units in front of it along the Z-axis. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 1.5, 8) looking at origin with OrbitControls for scene inspection. Add a warm DirectionalLight (0xffeedd) from above-left and soft AmbientLight (0x334455). Behind the sunglasses (at z=5), place a flat plane mesh acting as a 'retinal sensor' with an emissive material that changes color from green (safe) to red (dangerous) based on simulation results. Build an HTML overlay panel with these interactive controls: (1) a slider for 'Lens Tint Darkness' (0-100%) that adjusts sunglasses material opacity, (2) a slider for 'UV Filter Strength' (0-100%) affecting a numeric UV blocking parameter, (3) a rotation slider for 'Polarization Angle' (0-180 degrees) that rotates the sunglasses around their local Z-axis, (4) a distance slider (1-6 units) that moves the sunglasses closer or farther from the godrays source along Z, (5) a dropdown for 'Solar Intensity' with options Low/Medium/High/Extreme that scales the godrays model emissive brightness, and (6) a 'Run Analysis' button. When clicked, the button triggers a 2-second animated scan effect (a translucent plane sweeping from the godrays source through the sunglasses to the sensor). After the sweep, compute a protection score (0-100) based on weighted combination: tint contributes 30%, UV filter 30%, polarization alignment 20%, distance 20%, penalized by solar intensity. Display the score in a results box, color the sensor plane accordingly (green above 70, yellow 40-70, red below 40), and show a pass/fail verdict. Validate that all parameters have been adjusted from defaults before allowing analysis. Add a 'Reset' button as step 7 to restore all defaults. Use smooth GSAP-style tweens via Three.js AnimationMixer or manual lerping for all transitions.
